methods.name: Male Condom
methods.how_to_use: Roll onto erect penis before any genital contact. Hold tip to remove air. After ejaculation, withdraw while holding base.
methods.best_for: People wanting STI protection, occasional sex, or as backup method

methods.name: Female Condom
pros: Can be inserted hours before sex
methods.how_to_use: Insert closed end into vagina. Outer ring remains outside. Ensure penis enters sheath.
methods.best_for: Women wanting STI protection and control

methods.name: Combined Oral Contraceptive Pill
methods.name_swahili: Kidonge cha Uzazi wa Mpango Mseto
cons: Must take daily at same time
Not safe for some women (smokers >35, migraine with aura)
methods.how_to_use: Take one pill daily at same time. Start pack on day 1 of period or first Sunday after period.
methods.best_for: Women wanting highly effective, reversible method who can take daily pill

methods.name: Progestin-Only Pill (Mini-Pill)
pros: Safe for women who can't take estrogen
cons: Must take at exact same time daily (3-hour window)
methods.how_to_use: Take one pill at same time every day. No breaks between packs.
methods.best_for: Breastfeeding mothers, women with contraindications to estrogen

methods.name: Injectable (Depo-Provera)
pros: Private - nobody knows you're using it
cons: May delay return to fertility (6-12 months)
methods.how_to_use: Get injection from healthcare provider every 12-13 weeks.
methods.best_for: Women wanting private, infrequent dosing who don't plan pregnancy soon

methods.name: Implant (Jadelle/Implanon)
pros: Discrete - can't see or feel during sex
methods.how_to_use: Small rod inserted under skin of upper arm by trained provider. Remove when ready for pregnancy.
methods.best_for: Women wanting long-term, highly effective contraception without daily effort

methods.name: Copper IUD
pros: No hormones - no hormonal side effects
Can be used as emergency contraception
cons: May cause heavier, more painful periods
methods.how_to_use: T-shaped device inserted into uterus by provider. Check strings monthly.

methods.name: Hormonal IUD (Mirena)
pros: Lighter, less painful periods (may stop completely)
methods.how_to_use: T-shaped device inserted into uterus by provider. Releases local hormones.
methods.best_for: Women wanting long-term contraception with lighter periods

methods.name: Emergency Contraception (EC)
pros: Copper IUD as EC is 99% effective
cons: Only for emergencies - not regular use
methods.how_to_use: Take pill(s) as directed within 72 hours (120 hours for some brands) of unprotected sex.
methods.best_for: Emergency backup after condom break, missed pills, or unprotected sex

methods.name: Lactational Amenorrhea Method (LAM)
methods.how_to_use: Breastfeed exclusively (no formula/water) with less than 4-hour gaps day and night.
methods.best_for: Exclusively breastfeeding mothers in first 6 months

methods.name: Withdrawal Method
cons: High failure rate with typical use
methods.how_to_use: Penis withdrawn completely before ejaculation, away from vulva/vagina.
methods.best_for: Couples willing to accept higher failure risk; better than nothing

methods.name: Rhythm / Safe Days Method
methods.how_to_use: Track cycle length for 6+ months. Avoid sex on fertile days (days 8-19 of 28-day cycle).
methods.best_for: Women with very regular cycles willing to abstain or use backup during fertile window
